title: Decouple weight transport and lexicon integration to simplify loader lifecycle
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Background: Over the years the model ingestion pipeline accumulated ad-hoc coupling between weight transport/sharding logic and tokenizer/lexicon initialization. The current design forces the loader to hold shared mutable state for both weight activation and tokenizer vocabulary negotiation which increases tail latency, complicates streaming activation, and makes it hard to reason about format compatibility when we add new checkpoint variants.

Goal: Refactor the loader into two cooperating but independently deployable components: (1) a Weight Format Negotiator (WFN) responsible for format detection, shard manifest validation, and streaming-friendly transport adapters; and (2) a Tokenizer Bridge that performs lexicon negotiation and tokenizer bootstrap without blocking weight activation paths. The change should reduce warm-start and load-tail latency, make sharding semantics explicit, and permit pluggable support for future checkpoint formats without touching tokenizer internals.

Scope: This ticket implements the core refactor and migration scaffolding (API shims, compatibility tests, and a canary rollout plan). Follow-ons will split persistent caches and introduce a lightweight prefetch proxy. This work touches the loader service, artifact registry adapters, and unit/integration test harnesses.

Non-goals: Full removal of legacy checkpoint parsers (separate deprecation effort) and redesign of storage transport (S3/GCS) adapters beyond necessary interface changes.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a Weight Format Negotiator module with a deterministic format detection API and unit tests covering all supported checkpoint formats (hf, safetensors, custom-split)
Add a Tokenizer Bridge component that can initialize tokenizers from a lexicon proto without requiring loader global state
End-to-end integration tests verifying that streaming activation works when Tokenizer Bridge initializes asynchronously (no loader-level blocking > 50ms for activation path)
Model load tail latency reduced by >= 25% on our 95th percentile benchmark for large (70B+) models in staging
Backward compatibility tests demonstrating old checkpoint-only flow still works via an adapter shim
Canary rollout plan prepared and executed for 10% -> 50% -> 100% of model pushes with automated rollback on regressions
progress_notes: 2026-02-20: Ticket created. Spike performed by Diego to prototype format detection heuristics; prototyped stateless 'format sniff' that inspects manifest + first shard header. Outcome: reliable for current formats, edge-cases for split-checkpoints documented.

2026-02-25: Design review with IR and Tokenizer team. Decided to keep tokenizers immutable; Tokenizer Bridge will receive a lexicon proto and return a ready-to-use tokenizer handle. Lina to own implementation.

2026-03-02: PR #1842 opened implementing WFN with validators and unit tests. Early perf run shows a 12% drop in 95p model load tail; still short of target — next step: avoid synchronous lexicon validation during activation.

2026-03-08: Tokenizer Bridge PR #1851 adds async bootstrap and a compatibility shim that can operate in blocking mode for older model pushes. Integration tests added. Observed staging 95p tail improved to ~28% on 70B model set.

2026-03-10: Preparing canary rollout. Infra PR for routing ready. Need final sign-off from QA and SRE on rollback scripts. Remaining blockers: one flaky integration test (split-checkpoint reassembly) assigned to Eng-Infra.
